seed.everydayGoal: Roll a sheet of dough flat on the kitchen counter.
seed.normalExpectation: Pressing a rolling pin against dough makes the dough thinner and flatter beneath its barrel.
seed.impossibleRule: WHEN the rolling pin's barrel presses against dough, THE dough beneath the barrel ALWAYS forms a tall upright ridge instead of flattening.
seed.visibleTrigger: The rolling pin's horizontal barrel is pressed firmly against the top of the dough ridge.
seed.whyThisObject: A rolling pin applies broad pressure to flatten dough; the impossible response reverses that exact effect at the barrel's contact surface.
seed.goalRuleRelationship: Mimi needs a uniformly flat sheet, but the dough directly under the flattening tool stands upright as a thick ridge.
seed.frameZeroDescription: In a simple kitchen, Mimi stands behind a low counter, leaning forward with both hands on the handles of a horizontal rolling pin. Her straight arms press the barrel firmly against a thick, chest-high ridge of dough. The ridge is continuous with a broad sheet of dough spread across the counter, with thin, flat edges extending on either side. The rolling pin rests across the ridge's narrow top, far above those flat edges; the upright dough wall occupies the exact strip beneath its barrel.

source.sourceText: Roll a sheet of dough flat on the kitchen counter.

In a simple kitchen, Mimi stands behind a low counter, leaning forward with both hands on the handles of a horizontal rolling pin. Her straight arms press the barrel firmly against a thick, chest-high ridge of dough. The ridge is continuous with a broad sheet of dough spread across the counter, with thin, flat edges extending on either side. The rolling pin rests across the ridge's narrow top, far above those flat edges; the upright dough wall occupies the exact strip beneath its barrel.
WHEN the rolling pin's barrel presses against dough, THE dough beneath the barrel ALWAYS forms a tall upright ridge instead of flattening.
The rolling pin's horizontal barrel is pressed firmly against the top of the dough ridge.
